description:
The second READ at :93 reports '30', a permanent data error, after the first one succeeded. OPEN INPUT at :120 returns '00', the first READ takes the :94 arm and the record area is displayed twice - at :96 inside 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT and again at :78 in the mainline loop - and then the read that would otherwise have reported end of file reports '30' instead. Neither :94 nor :98 names that status, so :101 moves 12 into APPL-RESULT, 88 APPL-AOK is false at :104, 88 APPL-EOF is false at :107, and :110-113 run. Six lines, which is 4 + 2k for k = 1 record read. The point of the case is the four-character image. '30' IS numeric and IO-STAT1 is '3' rather than '9', so :162 falls through to the ELSE arm, :170 moves '0000' into IO-STATUS-04 and :171 overlays the status at one-based positions three and four, giving NNNN0030. The '23' case at this same call site and through this same paragraph (case10) must render a DIFFERENT image, so a renderer that hard-coded either four-character image, or that dropped the reference-modified (3:2) move, would satisfy one of the two and fail the other - which is what proves the digits are substituted from the actual IO-STATUS rather than written into the literal. The NNNN is itself part of the COBOL text at :168 and :172 and is not a placeholder awaiting substitution. No closing banner is expected: 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM displays 'ABENDING PROGRAM' at :155, moves 0 into TIMING at :156 and 999 into ABCODE at :157, and CALL 'CEE3ABD' at :158 does not return - so :83 never performs 9000-XREFFILE-CLOSE, the END OF EXECUTION line at :85 is never reached, and RETURN-CODE is 12. expectedWrites is empty because the program has no output dataset to write to at all, OPEN INPUT being the only open it performs whatever its prompt-mandated class name says; the seeded row is pinned as a whole fifty-byte image only, because the field-level decode of this exact row is already pinned field by field by case14. The failing status is named here in prose rather than in a member because ParityCase.ForcedOutcome belongs to ScreenRequest, which a BATCH_JOB case may not declare, so the arrangement lives in the scenario table of CBACT03CParityTest exactly as it does for case06 through case13. Every expected value is STATICALLY DERIVED from app/cbl/CBACT03C.cbl, app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy, app/jcl/READXREF.jcl and app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt rather than captured from a run of the legacy program, because this environment cannot execute COBOL (AAP 0.7.6, risk R-A).

HOW THE FAULT IS INDUCED, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. This case arranges a READ that fails after one record: unitStimulus.callSiteOutcomes names the call site READ-XREFFILE and gives it FILE STATUS '30', reported after 1 record(s) have been delivered. It is declared here because the identifier of a case must never configure it - a table in Java keyed by 'case01'..'case20' meant this file described three abend lines with nothing in it to say why, and renumbering a case silently changed what it did. A case that declares no call-site outcome runs clean, so silence here is itself a statement.
